body: Use `:set cursorline cursorlineopt=number`. This change was introduced to Vim in patch [8.1.2117](https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/49474ca12236776bb56aeb9d39bd6592e28157c7) to fix an issue, then ported to Neovim in #15226.
Maybe this is a documentation problem. <https://github.com/vim/vim/pull/8763>
I feel, this should be made the default.

@zeertzjq For certain filetypes like `netrw`, it is preferable to have the default style of `cursorline` set (i.e. the whole line highlighted). Is there a way to do this? A very hacky way would be:

```vim
  au FileType dirvish set cursorline cursorlineopt=both
```

But this also means that any file I open with netrw gives me the same cursorline for that filetype as well.
Maybe things can be easier if [8.1.2229](https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/efae76ab1a43d5a628d8c2fa4218ace6ba597f5d) is ported.

@paniash `'both'` (e.g. `'number,line'` is already the default).

EDIT: I misunderstood what you meant: I see that the line number is not highlighted when `'relativenumber'` is set but `'cursorline'` is unset.

> Maybe things can be easier if [8.1.2229](https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/efae76ab1a43d5a628d8c2fa4218ace6ba597f5d) is ported.

#15409
Now that #15409 has been merged, `:set winhighlight=LineNr:CursorLineNr` may be a workaround. (`LineNrAbove` and `LineNrBelow` are still linked to global `LineNr`).

issue.title: winhighlight / winhl doesn't affect groups that are linked to the overridden one

labels.name: closed:wontfix
labels.description: current behavior is by design, and change is not desired

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Neovim version (nvim -v)

0.5.1

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

does not apply

### Operating system/version

Arch Linux

### Terminal name/version

xfce4-terminal 0.8.10

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

system package manager

### How to reproduce the issue

echo 'foo bar' > foo
nvim --clean ./foo
:set termguicolors
:hi clear Normal
:hi clear NonText
:hi clear Foo
:syntax keyword Foo foo
:hi Normal guifg=#ff0000 guibg=#000000
:hi NonText guifg=#00ff00 guibg=#000000
:hi link Foo Normal
:set winhl=Normal:NonText

### Expected behavior

In the last step, _I_ expect that all text ("foo bar") becomes green, because `NonText` is green, and it overrides `Normal` (due to `winhl`), so all `Normal` text (" bar") should be in green, but not just that, all text whose highlighting group _links_ to `Normal` ("foo" is `Foo`, which links to `Normal`) should all be in green as well.

### Actual behavior

The implementation of `winhighlight` currently doesn't seem to follow links and only applies to groups directly, that means that the `winhighlight` overrides does half of the job, and hence, makes " bar" green (because it's `Normal` text, which gets overridden) but keeps "foo" in red (which is `Foo` that links to `Normal`).

https://github.com/neoclide/coc.nvim/issues/1251
